fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. "…Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he." (Job 32:4). He kept waiting until he saw that the three men had no further reply, and then his anger was kindled (Job 32:5). That's a lot of patience for one man.

Power never comes up in Elihu's words. He says, "It is not only the old who are wise…" (Job 32:9). Nobody in this speech is asking about a title or a corner office. I think a powerful person with no wisdom is just a loud person in a nice chair.
